text.p: Leaders of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum hold their fourth annual summit at Subic Bay, near Manila, on Monday. Following are key APEC dates:

1989, Canberra - First ministerial meeting as an informal dialogue group of 12 trading partners in the world's fastest growing area. The 12 countries represented were Australia, Brunei, Canada, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, New Zealand, Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Thailand, United States.

1991, Seoul - Third ministerial meeting. The Seoul Declaration said APEC economies would work for more open trade, greater economic cooperation, investment expansion and a stronger mutilateral trading system. China, Hong Kong and Taiwan (known in APEC as Chinese Taipei) admitted as members.
1992, Bangkok - Fourth ministerial meeting. Mexico and Papua New Guinea admitted as members

1993, Seattle - Fifth ministerial meeting and first APEC Economic Leaders Meeting (AELM) -- summit -- hosted by U.S. President Bill Clinton. The summit called for a "deepening of the spirit of community in the Asia-Pacific" and provided impetus for making the region more integrated economically. Chile admitted as a member and a three-year moratorium on new membership imposed.

1994, Jakarta - Sixth ministerial meeting. Second summit at Bogor, near Jakarta, adopted the goal of free and open trade and investment in the region by 2010 for industrialised economies and 2020 for developing economies.
1995, Osaka - Seventh ministerial meeting. Summit endorsed Osaka Action Agenda, a blueprint of actions to accomplish the Bogor goals.

1996, Manila - Eighth ministerial meeting, Nov 22-23. Summit Nov 25 at nearby Subic Bay to endorse Manila Action Plan (MAP) adopted by ministers integrating individual action plans of member economies, and a separate document entitled a "Declaration of Principles on Economic Cooperation and Development in the APEC Region". The three-year membership moratorium will be allowed to lapse but no new members to be admitted until 1999.
